purpose: Test how quickly network movement weakens when critical roads fail cumulatively.

mathematical_formulation.stress_tolerance: A_R is the normalised trapezoidal area under Q_k over the tested sequence
mathematical_formulation.thresholds: Return the first tested k with Q_k <= 0.90, 0.75 and 0.50, plus the first increase in weakly connected components

sequence_rule: Use the confirmed current critical-road order when supplied; otherwise compute the deterministic single-road efficiency-loss ranking and remove roads cumulatively.

primary_sources.citation: Scott, Novak, Aultman-Hall and Guo (2006), Network Robustness Index: A new method for identifying critical links and evaluating the performance of transportation networks
Nagurney and Qiang (2008), A network efficiency measure with application to critical infrastructure networks. Journal of Global Optimization, 40, 261-275.
Jenelius, Petersen and Mattsson (2006), Importance and exposure in road network vulnerability

verification_contract: each road removed at most once
curve is non-increasing within numerical tolerance
thresholds refer only to tested stages
known_limitations: This targeted sequence is not a road-failure probability model.
Topology efficiency does not represent congestion or demand-weighted delay.
A missing threshold means it was not reached within the requested positive Top-N, not that it can never occur.
